subject_entity.notes: Student of Origen; bishop of Alexandria c. 248–264; key figure in the Trinitarian controversies after Origen; opposed Sabellianism but was himself accused of tritheism; major voice during the Decian persecution and the Novatian controversy; extensive correspondence preserved by Eusebius.

object_entity.notes: Major Egyptian port city; intellectual and commercial center; seat of the Catechetical School; major Christian center from the first century onward.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Origen, while still very young, succeeded Clement as head of the Catechetical School in Alexandria; so many came to him, both men and women, that a multitude of heretics and not a few of the most distinguished philosophers attended his instruction; he led many to the faith and some to martyrdom.

subject_entity.notes: Origen's systematic theological work composed in Alexandria c. 220–230; the first attempt at a comprehensive Christian theology; four books covering God and the Trinity, the created world, free will, and Scripture; source for the doctrines of eternal generation of the Son, pre-existence of souls, universal restoration (apokatastasis), and allegorical exegesis; preserved mostly through Rufinus's sanitized Latin translation and fragments in Justinian's condemnation.
